title: fix(service-automation): get_record names id in the projection it hands the engine, so output.id is the row id whatever fields names
body:
Fixes #22344

Clause-②: no

A `get_record` node's single-row (`findOne`) branch answers `output: { record, id, object }`, and a later node reads that `id` as `{read.id}`. The node handed the author's `fields` to the engine unchanged, and the SQL drivers return exactly the columns a projection names, so a projection without `id` answered `output.id` undefined with no error. The branch now names `id` in the projection it hands the engine.

## Measured first: the defect is real on `main` (H1)

Measured on `origin/main` `35afb1587` plus the red-first test commit `4abddae9a`, through the real `ObjectQL` (`ObjectKernel` + `ObjectQLPlugin`) and the registered `get_record` executor, `runAs: 'system'`, one row `{ title: 'alpha', status: 'open' }`:

| driver | `fields` | `output.id` | `record` keys |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `driver-sql` (better-sqlite3 `:memory:`) | `['title']` | `undefined` | `[title]` |
| `driver-sql` | absent | the row id | all 10 columns, `id` included |
| `driver-memory` | `['title']` | the row id | `[id, title]` |
| `driver-memory` | absent | the row id | all 5 columns |

The memory row is the contrast: its `projectFields` adds `id` to every projection itself, so the defect showed on the SQL drivers only. The flow-level shape the card names was red too: `start → get_record(fields: ['title']) → update_record(filter: { id: '{read.id}' })` was refused with `update_record: refusing to run — 1 filter condition(s) resolved to nothing and were dropped from the query: {read.id} (at id)`.

## Where `id` is added (H2)

`projectionNamingId(fields)` in `builtin/crud-nodes.ts` returns the author's `fields` with `id` appended, and the `findOne` branch hands that to `serveFamilyRead` as the node's projection:

- a projection that already names `id` is handed over as written, so `id` is never doubled;
- `fields` absent or `[]` is returned unchanged, so a whole-row read stays a whole-row read and no projection is invented;
- the `find` branch (`limit > 1`) does not call it and is byte-unchanged.

Placement, measured: adding `id` before `serveFamilyRead` (shipped) and adding it inside the projection callback (`fields: projectionNamingId(projection)`, a one-off mutation, not committed) give the same answers on both paths, 23/23 across the three `get_record` suites at `f6e3ac4ba`. On the stored-metadata path the family projection only adds and then drops `type`, and `id` survives either way. Before `serveFamilyRead` is the shipped form so that the family door sees the node's whole projection as the node's own, instead of a column it does not know about arriving after it decided.

## `record` carries `id` when the author did not name it (H3)

The record the node serves, and binds to its `outputVariable`, carries the `id` the engine returned beside the named columns. The reasons:

- the engine returned it, and taking it back off would be a second projection layer over the engine's answer;
- `{rec.id}` through the `outputVariable` then agrees with `{read.id}`; stripping it would leave the same defect on the variable spelling, which an author is as likely to write;
- every other single-row read already carries it: an unprojected read on every driver, and every projected read on `driver-memory` (table above).

Two existing pins asserted the exact column set on the single-row branch, and each now expects the named columns plus `id`:

- `get-record-stored-metadata-family.integration.test.ts`: the body-without-type projection now serves `[checksum, id, metadata, name]`, and `type` is still taken back off;
- `get-record-formula-projection.integration.test.ts`, which landed with PR #22337 while this branch was open (merged in from `origin/main` `54c3ce10c`): the `one` branch cases now include `id: 'line_1'`, and the `list` branch cases are unchanged. That PR's engine-level trimming is untouched. Its `fields` projection is now handed to the engine with `id` named, which the trim honours.

## Pins (H4), `get-record-id-projection.integration.test.ts`

- control: the SQL driver returns exactly the named columns (`{ title: 'alpha' }`);
- `fields` omitting `id`: `output.id` is the row id, `record` is `{ id, title }`, and the engine was handed `['title', 'id']` (red on `main`);
- `fields` naming `id`: handed as written (`['id', 'title']`), so `id` appears once;
- control, no `fields` and `fields: []`: no projection is invented, and `output` equals `{ record: WHOLE_ROW, id, object }` with the engine's own whole-row answer as `WHOLE_ROW`;
- flow level: `update_record` filtering on `{read.id}` after a narrowed `get_record` closes exactly that row, and `rec` is `{ id, title }` (red on `main`).

## Ablation, one-off, after the fix was committed (no permanent mutation file)

Each leg was run through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode. Each anchor hit once, the mutation was verified on disk (anchor count and blob hash), and the restore was proven: the blob equals `HEAD` (`94641f32745d`) and `git diff HEAD` is empty, with a belt `trap` on `EXIT INT TERM`. The subject is imported from source (`./crud-nodes.js`), so no `dist/` leg applies. Final run at `f6e3ac4ba` over the three `get_record` suites:

| leg | mutation | result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| M1 | `return [...fields, 'id']` replaced by `return fields` (fix reverted) | 7 red: omit-id, flow `{read.id}`, family projection, and the 4 formula `one` cases |
| M2 | the `fields.includes('id')` guard dropped | 1 red: id-named, handed `['id', 'title', 'id']` |
| M3b | the `fields.length === 0` guard dropped | 1 red: empty control, handed `['id']` |
| M4 | absent `fields` answered `['id']` | 6 red: no-fields control plus 5 whole-row reads in the family suite |
| H2-alt | `id` added inside the callback instead | 23/23 green (a placement measurement, not an ablation) |

The first M3 attempt at `d6ccba323` was a no-op. Its replacement text was a substring of its anchor, so `ablation-replace` refused it (replacement count 1 to 1) and never ran the tests. It was re-anchored as M3b and run.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` at `f6e3ac4ba`: 178 files / 2177 tests passed. At `d6ccba323`, before the merge, it was 177 / 2169.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation run typecheck` at `f6e3ac4ba`: `tsc --noEmit` clean. `check:test-typecheck` OK, 0 files / 0 errors; `tsconfig.test.json` includes `src/**/*`, so the new test is compiled.
- `f68b7d55c` changes only the changeset's wording against `f6e3ac4ba` (`git diff --stat`: one file, `.changeset/`).
- Targeted eslint (`--no-inline-config`, `--format json`) on the 4 changed `.ts` files: 4 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. All 4 fall under the `packages/**/*.{ts,…}` config objects (`--print-config` resolves each). The config enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`, per `eslint.config.mjs`), so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.
- Gate families: 64 families derived by `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (no paths) at `f68b7d55c`; all 64 run there and all 64 exited 0. `--ran` reconciliation: `64 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 64 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero — all 64 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3)`. The first pass at `d6ccba323` read `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` as PREREQUISITE NOT MET (no workspace `dist/`). After this package was built it passed: `106 published require entry point(s) across 66 package(s) load`. CI's own jobs were not run locally: Test Core, Dogfood, Temporal, Build Core, the workspace type-check lanes, and the roster and wide-population families that `dispatch-gates` names outside its 64.

## Acceptance notes

- `GetRecordConfigSchema.fields` (spec) and the descriptor's `configSchema` describe `fields` as "only these fields are read (default: all)". On the single-row branch the served record now also carries `id`. `packages/spec` is outside this card, and the descriptor carries the same sentence as the spec, so neither was edited. A wording follow-up would name `id` there. Owner: none; `domain:services` seat to decide.
- The `find` branch (`limit > 1`) declares no top-level `id`. Its rows still carry only the named columns on the SQL drivers when `fields` omits `id`. That is the author's projection, and this PR leaves it unchanged by the card's scope.
- `driver-mongodb` was not measured, because the package's tests do not depend on it.
